name: Parshuram Kund
description: Major Hindu pilgrimage site on the banks of the Lohit River in the Mishmi plateau area, associated with Sage Parashurama washing away the sin of matricide. Attracts tens of thousands of devotees during Makar Sankranti for holy dips.
facts: Located approximately 48 km from Tezu via Tohangam within Kamlang Reserve Forest area.
Annual Parshuram Mela held in January draws pilgrims from across India and Nepal.
Coordinates verified from Wikipedia and OSM sources as 27°52′39″N 96°21′33″E.
Site reformed after 1950 Assam earthquake with circular boulder formation in the riverbed.

name: Tezu
description: Headquarters town of Lohit district and gateway to the Lohit Valley, serving as base for Parshuram Kund, Glow Lake and Mishmi cultural experiences. Known for secular harmony with temple, monastery and gurudwara in the same compound.
facts: Elevation about 185 m; on the banks of the Lohit River.
Mishmi tribes maintain traditional king and queen residence in the area.
Tezu Airport (TEI) provides connectivity; nearest major airport Dibrugarh.
Ideal base for river rafting, hiking and visits to nearby spiritual and nature sites.

name: Glow Lake (Glaw Tuwi)
description: Pristine high-altitude freshwater lake inside Kamlang Wildlife Sanctuary near Wakro, accessible only by trek. Surrounded by dense evergreen forests, orchids and Himalayan flora; recently designated India's 101st Ramsar Site.
facts: Elevation approximately 1,168 m; area about 8 sq km or 129 ha per Ramsar data.
Coordinates from Ramsar Information Sheet: 27°41'47"N 96°27'11"E.
Trek from Wakro takes 5–8 hours through forests and streams; local Mishmi guides recommended.
First Ramsar Site in Arunachal Pradesh; headwaters of Kamlang River.

name: Kamlang Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area covering 783 sq km in southern Lohit, home to tigers, clouded leopards, Mishmi takin and rich orchid diversity. Contains Glow Lake and borders Namdapha National Park; one of India's tiger reserves.
facts: Established 1989; coordinates approximate centre from Wikipedia 27°40′N 96°26′E.
Northern boundary Lang River; southern border with Namdapha.
Nearest town Wakro; supports all four big cats found in India in the broader landscape.
Ideal for birdwatching, orchid viewing and eco-tourism with proper permits.

name: Wakro
description: Circle headquarters village and gateway to Kamlang Wildlife Sanctuary and Glow Lake, known for Mishmi culture, orange orchards and scenic hills. Serves as starting point for Glow Lake treks.
facts: Population about 1,215 (2011 Census); primarily Mishmi people.
Coordinates from Wikipedia: 27°46′59″N 96°20′52″E.
Connected by NH-13 and NH-15; PIN 792102.
Base for Glow Lake trek and visits to Parshuram Kund nearby.

name: Lohit View Point (Tohangam)
description: Scenic viewpoint on rocky hills at Tohangam, about 32 km from Tezu on the road toward Hayuliang, offering panoramic sunrise and sunset views of the Lohit Valley.
facts: Officially listed by Lohit district NIC as a top tourist destination.
Approximate coordinates based on Tohangam village/post office data.
Ideal for dry picnic and photography of the magnificent Lohit valley.
On the historic route toward eastern frontier areas.

name: District Museum and Craft Centre (Tezu)
description: Cultural centre in Tezu showcasing books, crafts, handloom and artefacts of Mishmi, Khamti and other communities of Arunachal Pradesh.
facts: Listed among main attractions of Tezu by official district tourism page.
Houses traditional textiles, tribal art and ethnographic displays.
Central location in Tezu makes it easily accessible for visitors.

name: Buddha Vihar (Chong, Tezu)
description: Local Buddhist monastery known as Chong in Tezu, serving the Buddhist community with prayer halls, golden Buddha statue and cultural gatherings of Khamti and Mishmi tribes.
facts: Official district tourism lists Buddha-Vihar among Tezu's main attractions.
Locally called Chong; hosts community events and daily rituals.
Part of the secular complex atmosphere in Tezu alongside temple and gurudwara.

name: Lohit River
description: Major tributary of the Brahmaputra flowing through Lohit district, offering river rafting, angling, scenic riverside views and the sacred setting for Parshuram Kund.
facts: District named after the river; flows past Tezu and Parshuram Kund.
Popular for river rafting and angling from Tezu base.
Forms the sacred Brahmakund area linked to Parashurama legend.

name: Pakke Tiger Reserve
description: Project Tiger reserve covering about 862 sq km in the foothills, renowned as Hornbill country with four species of hornbills, tigers, elephants and high biodiversity. Formerly Pakhui Wildlife Sanctuary, it supports community-based conservation including the Hornbill Nest Adoption Programme.
facts: Coordinates from Wikipedia: 27°05′N 92°51.5′E.
Core area 861.95 sq km; elevations 150-2000 m.
Won India Biodiversity Award 2016 for Hornbill Nest Adoption Programme.
Bounded by Kameng and Pakke Rivers; access via Seijosa from Tezpur.
Hosts over 300 bird species and 40 mammals.

name: Lemmi
description: Headquarters town of Pakke-Kessang district, known for Nyishi tribal culture, dance festivals and as an administrative and cultural hub near the Papum Pare boundary.
facts: District HQ since formation in 2018 from East Kameng.
Coordinates approx 27°09′36″N 93°13′12″E from Wikipedia.
Hosts tribal dance festivals; connected via NH-13.
Gateway for cultural experiences of Nyishi, Galo and Puroik communities.

name: Seijosa
description: Circle headquarters and gateway town along the Pakke River, popular picnic and base location for Pakke Tiger Reserve visits, with frequent sightings of hornbills, elephants and birds in surrounding foothills.
facts: Main access point to Pakke Tiger Reserve from Tezpur (about 64 km).
Site of annual Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival promoting conservation.
Coordinates approximate from GeoNames/Seijosa ADC data.
Community eco-camps and forest rest houses available nearby.

name: Pakke-Kessang Hill Station
description: Scenic cool-climate area in Pakke Valley offering panoramic Himalayan views, lush green valleys, meandering rivers and paddy fields; ideal for offbeat hill retreats.
facts: Located about 140-144 km from Seppa; cooler winters.
Part of the Three Valleys (Pakke, Passa, Pappu) scenic landscape.
Coordinates approximate matching the town listing.
Inspection bungalows available for visitors.

name: Naksaparvat (Naksha Parbat)
description: Medieval archaeological site (13th–16th century) with fortified settlement ruins, brick and stone structures, wells and ramparts on the left bank of the Borgang River, associated with Chutia kingdom hill forts.
facts: Located in Dissing Passo circle, Pakke-Kessang district.
Coordinates from Wikipedia: approx 26°57′35″N 93°10′12″E.
One of the few systematically excavated medieval sites in Arunachal Pradesh.
Features stone plinths, pillars and evidence of iron-working.

name: Passa Valley (Rilloh)
description: Picturesque valley and tourist village area known for scenic riverbanks, open landscapes, paddy fields and views from road tops, part of the district's northern attractions.
facts: Rilloh tourist village about 78 km south of Seppa.
Passa Valley covers northern district from Pijerang to Lumdung and Rilloh.
Ideal for drives and nature viewing; Inspection Bungalows available.
Listed among notable attractions by Wikipedia and district sources.

name: Lumdung
description: Area known as wintering grounds for certain migratory bird species, set in the scenic Passa Valley with green landscapes in summer.
facts: Popular for migratory birds during winter season.
Located in Passa Valley region of the district.
Part of the Three Valleys scenic circuit from Seppa.
Official sources note its birdwatching potential.

name: Pakke River
description: Major river flowing through the district, known for fishing (with permits), scenic riverside views, picnic spots near Seijosa and as the eastern boundary of the tiger reserve.
facts: Requires permits from district headquarters for fishing.
Forms eastern boundary of Pakke Tiger Reserve.
Seijosa lies along its banks; popular for picnics.
Supports local ecology and tourism activities.

name: Pakke Jungle Camp
description: Community-based eco-tourism camp near Seijosa on the fringes of Pakke Tiger Reserve, run with local Nyishi groups, offering jungle stays, birdwatching and low-impact conservation-linked accommodation.
facts: Implemented by Help Tourism and local self-help group Ghora-Aabhe.
Located near Seijosa; basic cottages overlooking forest canopy.
Supports conservation and provides local employment.
Ideal for immersive nature and hornbill experiences.
